subject: accountancy
method: Independent blind solve saved to accountancy-blind-solutions.json before opening the separate key file. All 15 stems, ordered choices, explanations and source locators then audited. Model receipts were not used as truth.
scope: Current passing 15-question Accountancy snapshot only; artifact-only audit, no bank/DB/registry/content mutation.

verdict_definition.approve: No blocking academic/mapping/source defect found; listed improvements may still be useful.
verdict_definition.suspect: Withhold strict approval until stated condition, mapping, formatting, or source-entailment defect is repaired and rechecked.
verdict_definition.incomplete: Required evidence unavailable; no academic decision.

bank_level_findings: All 15 intended keys match the blind solve; two matching/numerical questions are still conditional and cannot be certified merely from matching keys.
Three share-capital questions are incorrectly labelled Financial Statements of Company. Two fixed-capital posting questions should be remapped to Partnership Fundamentals for exact topic routing.
The 15 rows cover a narrow group of repeatedly adapted anchors q3,q5,q7,q14,q17,q20; this is not broad Accountancy syllabus coverage.
Format labels for numerical and journal-entry questions vary and should be standardised separately from academic correctness.
Do not claim zero errors, a numerical perfection grade, or 2027-final syllabus validation from this audit.

reasons: 600 is correct only if the final call is the sole unpaid capital instalment. Fully called-up means demanded, not received; the stem does not explicitly state all other capital instalments were paid.

For example, if a further Rs 4 capital instalment had also been unpaid, capital received would be Rs 3 per share and 1,400 shares would also fit Rs 4,200. The current explanation silently assumes Rs 7 received.
